fields.headline: 'Flight 666 to Purgatory': Hacked screens, stranded bags throw NCIA into chaos
fields.dek: Airport officials have not said whether the outage was a cyberattack. Travelers are being told to check their airline apps.
fields.heroImageBrief: passengers silhouetted under rows of departure boards in an airport terminal, editorial press photo
fields.heroCaption: Travelers wait beneath departure boards in the main terminal at Northeast Central Interstate Airport on Tuesday as staff directed passengers by hand.
fields.body:
CLEVELAND — Departure screens at Northeast Central Interstate Airport began showing flights to "PURGATORY" and "NOWHERE" late Tuesday morning, sending travelers to gates that did not exist and leaving checked bags piled up beneath Concourse A.

By noon, some passengers said they had walked between three different gates for the same flight. "The board said A1, the app said A12, and nobody at either gate knew anything," said Dave Kowalski, who was trying to reach Atlanta.

Two airline employees, who asked not to be named because they were not authorized to speak publicly, said the baggage system serving Concourse A stopped around 10:30 a.m. A Transportation Security Administration source said screening was briefly paused.

An airport spokesperson said NCIA was "investigating a technical issue" and that there was no threat to aircraft. The spokesperson did not say whether the problem was a cyberattack.

A post claiming terrorists had seized the control tower was shared hundreds of times on Facebook before noon. The Federal Aviation Administration said air traffic control was operating normally.
